newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY SEAFOODS TAKES H1 PROVISION.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY SEAFOODS TAKES H1 PROVISION.

text.p: Norway Seafoods ASA, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, said on Tuesday it had taken a provision in the first half of the year of 400 million crowns for restructuring costs.
The company said it booked 250 million crowns as ordinary operating expenses and 150 million crowns as extraordinary costs.
Norway Seafoods is 60 percent owned by Norwegian holding company Aker RGI ASA.

It posted a first-half operating loss of 129 million crowns, versus a profit of 58 million crowns in the same year-ago period, and a pre-tax loss of 313 million crowns, against a 102 million crowns profit.

Norway Seafoods said that due to poor earnings in the first half of the year, its management had decided to implement a new strategy with the focus on the building up of brand products and prioritising markets.

The strategy will entail the reorganisation and restructuring of the group, especially land-based activities in Europe, the United States and Asia, and catching operations in South America, Norway Seafoods said.
